179.t: Brother's instruments, nephews and the Bocage family tree

179.ch: Peter's band and the Bocage family
179.q: he even had, he played this, uh, soprano. Mm-hmm. He had, he longed that soprano, though, to, to Teo, who had died. I believe Teo had that clarinet, that soprano, until he died.

567.t: The Matthews brothers and how parades have changed
567.s: Talk about the Matthews brothers (Bill, Happy and the bass drummer), White visiting them, and how parades now invite trouble.
567.ch: Second lining and the brass bands

He stays on, uh, he stays on Appaloosa Street. Appaloosa between, uh, Socrack and the Shadows Street. So I'll be, I'll be with him all. I'll be, used…

909.s: Morris recalls trombonist Johnny and drummer Joe Lindsay, brothers who could not get along; the tape is nearly out.
909.q: Johnny Lindsay from uptown. Johnny Lindsay, Joe Lindsay. Now, Johnny Lindsay used to play trombone. You sure know him all right. You keep up with him better than me.

437.t: Darius Brubeck and the Brubeck sons
437.s: He played with Darius Brubeck on trombone, comments on the pressure of a famous father, and mentions Danny and Paul Desmond's saxophone.
437.ch: Playing styles, cruises and tribute bands
437.q: Yes. Like I say I am versatile and jazz is my music but I bring something from all these experiences into my playing. I was doing a big band show with what I’ll call a vintage big band, it was playing a concert. And I looked to my left and there was Darius Brubeck playing trombone. And an excellent…

323.t: Brothers Peter and Frank, no sibling rivalry
323.s: His brothers played too; Frank followed the Whiteman band, circus and ice shows. They respected each other.
323.q: Yeah, both brothers, Peter and Frank. Frank is still alive. He lives in Riverside, California. He still plays whatever is left of the music business. He did the same thing I did, the Whiteman band, the circus, the ice shows and so forth.

348.s: Abe and Sam play together in his big band; they were distant for years but became buddies in Los Angeles.
348.q: As a matter of fact we’re doing — every time I do the big band thing I have fifteen men, I have six brass, five saxes and three rhythm, four rhythm sometimes when I add a guitar, and Sam comes out and does a scat thing that he and I play flute and clarinet.

452.t: How Illinois treated his brother Russell
452.s: Cobb says that once Illinois formed his own band he mistreated Russell, who could have been better with proper support, and cites the Polo Grounds game snub.
452.q: So after this happened, Illinois left Cab Calloway's AND FORMED A BAND band, and told us we were gonna have a band together. Together. Russell

383.t: Brother Gus's arranging and Sy Oliver
383.s: Wilson says he hasn't heard from Gus in fifteen years, and recalls Gus's arranging in the Speed Webb band and friendship with Sy Oliver.
383.q: Uh-huh. James Augustus, that was my older brother. He was a junior, that was my father's name, James Augustus. I lost track -- I haven't heard from my brother 15 years now. I doubt if he's alive, but nobody in the family's heard from him. My mother died about 13 years ago and no one was able to get…

78.t: Rebutting claims of resentment between Horace and Fletcher
78.s: Horace says he never resented Fletcher musically; their only quarrels were about Fletcher not worrying whether the band showed up. He also denies rebuffing researchers, saying he's easy to find.
78.ch: Setting the record straight on Hendersonia
78.q: This is the first I've ever heard of that, and I'm actually surprised, because Leonard and I are great friends, and Leonard --
